faq.q: Why use Ti-65 for titanium hypersonic control surface?
faq.a: Ti-65 high-temperature titanium alloy maintains structural strength up to 650C for hypersonic vehicle control surfaces and high-speed aerospace applications.

faq.q: How is a titanium hypersonic control surface manufactured?
faq.a: A typical titanium hypersonic control surface is manufactured using Closed-die forging; 5-axis CNC machining; Heat treatment (STA); Shot peening. BOZE CNC Ti uses precision CNC equipment with strict process controls to ensure consistent quality and dimensional accuracy.

faq.q: What are the alternatives to Ti-65 for titanium hypersonic control surface?
faq.a: Alternative materials include stainless steel (heavier, susceptible to corrosion) and aluminum (lower strength, shorter fatigue life). The alternative manufacturing method is Machining from solid billet (90%+ material waste, no grain flow optimization).

faq.q: What standards apply to titanium hypersonic control surface?
faq.a: Titanium Hypersonic Control Surface components are typically manufactured to ASTM B348, ASME. Additional customer-specific specifications may apply.

faq.q: What are common failure modes for titanium hypersonic control surface?
faq.a: Common failure modes include Surface contamination from iron pickup during machining requiring acid passivation (ASTM F86). BOZE CNC Ti mitigates these through strict process control, proper material selection, and 100% inspection.

faq.q: What is the typical lead time for custom titanium hypersonic control surface?
faq.a: Standard lead time is 2-4 weeks depending on quantity and complexity. Rush orders can be accommodated. Contact our sales team for specific delivery schedules.
